payload.prompt: What do speech capabilities process?

options.rationale: Speech capabilities work with spoken language. Recognition and synthesis handle its input or output.
Written text can feed synthesis, but it is not the whole scope. Speech capabilities also handle spoken input or output.
options.better_fit: Written text is the input for speech synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: This would leave out spoken input.
feedback.instructional: Speech capabilities concern spoken language through recognition and synthesis.

options.rationale: Storing audio does not understand or generate language. It is distinct from speech conversion.
options.better_fit: Audio storage is useful for retaining recordings.

feedback.intrinsic: A recording alone would not create a transcript or reply.
feedback.instructional: Recognition and synthesis perform the language conversions.

options.rationale: Phoneme probabilities can occur inside recognition. They do not describe the complete speech capability.

feedback.intrinsic: This omits usable text and spoken output.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Speech capabilities work with spoken language.

payload.prompt: Which are speech capabilities? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech recognition is a speech capability. It converts spoken words to text.
Speech synthesis is a speech capability. It converts text to spoken audio.
Text-to-speech is another name for synthesis. It speaks written information.
Audio capture supplies a digital audio signal. It does not itself convert between speech and text.
options.better_fit: It is an early step before recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: Captured audio alone produces neither transcript nor response.
feedback.instructional: Recognition and synthesis are the conversion capabilities.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Recognition and synthesis are speech capabilities.

payload.prompt: A voice-service team needs callers to speak questions and hear spoken answers. Which plan should the designer choose?

options.rationale: Recognition converts callers' speech into text. Synthesis speaks the response text aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The caller would not hear an answer.
feedback.instructional: Two-way voice interaction needs recognition for input and synthesis for output.

options.rationale: Synthesis can speak a prepared response. It cannot understand the caller's question.
options.better_fit: It fits an app that only announces information.

feedback.intrinsic: The service would not know what the caller asked.
feedback.instructional: Recognition is needed to process spoken requests.

options.rationale: Capture records sound as data. It neither transcribes questions nor speaks answers.
options.better_fit: It fits the input stage before recognition.

payload.prompt: What does speech recognition do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Recognition takes spoken language as input. It begins with captured speech.
Producing written text from speech is recognition's core role. It is therefore called speech-to-text.
A transcription gives an app usable written content. That supports understanding a spoken request.
Reading text aloud is speech synthesis. Recognition moves from speech to text instead.
options.better_fit: It fits text-to-speech.

feedback.intrinsic: No written transcript would be produced.
feedback.instructional: Recognition listens and writes; synthesis speaks.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Recognition listens to speech and produces text.

payload.prompt: What is another name for speech recognition?

options.rationale: Speech recognition changes spoken language into written text. Speech-to-text names that direction.
Text-to-speech changes written text into audio. That is synthesis rather than recognition.
options.better_fit: It is another name for speech synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: A spoken request would not be transcribed.
feedback.instructional: Speech-to-text listens and writes.

options.rationale: A neural vocoder generates audio waveforms in synthesis. It does not transcribe speech.
options.better_fit: It fits a waveform-generation stage of synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: The needed written words would not appear.
feedback.instructional: Vocoding belongs to audio generation, not recognition.

options.rationale: Text normalization prepares written text for pronunciation. It does not convert speech into text.
options.better_fit: It fits a synthesis text-preparation stage.

payload.prompt: Which are benefits of speech-enabled experiences? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech can reduce reliance on keyboards and screens. This enables hands-free operation.
Speech can be used while another task continues. This supports multitasking.
Speaking and hearing can feel conversational. This can make interactions more natural.
